name: Pointer Gestures
explanation: Some features rely on a multi-finger gesture, like pinch-to-zoom, or a path-based gesture, like swiping in a specific direction. Those features must also work with a single-pointer action that doesn't require following a path, such as a plain tap or click on a button. The path itself is what's off-limits as the only option, not multi-touch or dragging in general. A photo viewer that only zooms via pinch needs to also offer zoom-in and zoom-out buttons, for instance. An exception applies when the gesture itself is essential to the specific function, such as a signature pad or a freehand drawing tool.
whoItAffects: Some people can't reliably perform a precise pinch or a smooth swipe. This can happen with motor disabilities that affect fine motor control, even if the person can tap a button just fine. People using a single-switch device or a mouth stick can't perform multi-touch gestures at all. Those gestures need more than one point of contact at once. A single-tap alternative keeps the feature usable no matter how precise the input method is.
howToTest: On a touchscreen device, find any feature that responds to a pinch or a swipe. Pinch-to-zoom and swiping to dismiss a card are two examples. For each one, check whether the same result can also come from a simple tap or click, like a visible zoom button or a next/previous arrow. Suppose the gesture is the only way to trigger that function, and it isn't essential to the activity. This fails.

check.question: A mobile photo gallery app lets users swipe left or right to move between photos, and this is the only way to navigate; there are no visible next/previous buttons as an alternative. Does this pass SC 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures?
choices: Yes, because swiping is a standard, widely understood gesture on touchscreens
No, because the path-based swipe gesture has no single-pointer alternative like a tap-based button
Yes, because photo galleries are exempt from this criterion
It depends only on how many photos are in the gallery
